gen_risks.description: Electricity tariffs set below the cost of service create severe sector financial deficits and reliance on subsidies, threatening power sector utility viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support tariff reform strategies and analytical studies on utility financial viability during project implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: The current electricity price is below the cost of service causing financial difficulties for sector utilities.

gen_risks.description: Transmission capacity constraints on the single-circuit 220kV Baganuur-Choir corridor prevent evacuation of existing renewable power and block new renewable connections.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct a new 220kV double-circuit transmission line from Baganuur to Choir Substation and expand associated substations.
gen_risks.evidence: its output is constrained due to the limit of the transmission capacity of the Baganuur-Choir 220kV single-circuit line

gen_risks.description: An aging coal-fired CHP generation fleet lacks operational flexibility, hindering system dispatch and integration of variable renewable energy.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen grid infrastructure, deploy battery energy storage systems, and provide technical assistance for variable renewable energy integration.
gen_risks.evidence: The CHP plants make the power system inflexible, making it indispatchable and difficult to integrate Variable Renewable Energy

gen_risks.description: Construction and operation of overhead high-voltage transmission lines present collision hazards and habitat disturbance for local bird populations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Realign the transmission line routing to avoid wetland habitats, install bird flight diverters, and implement a Bird Management Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Transmission lines in Mongolia often involve bird collision and other biodiversity issues

gen_risks.description: A newly established PMO lacking experience with World Bank fiduciary and operational procedures creates risks of implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire an Owner's Engineer to assist the PMO and conduct early World Bank training on procurement, financial management, and safeguards.
gen_risks.evidence: Previous infrastructure projects in Mongolia have experienced implementation delays due to the administrative and technical capacity constraints of the implementing agencies.

gen_risks.description: The short local construction season in Mongolia means civil works delays prior to winter can postpone project completion by an entire year.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate advance procurement planning to begin works early in the season and use rated criteria evaluating contractors' short-season delivery plans.
gen_risks.evidence: If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays with waiting for the next construction season.

gen_risks.description: Heavy dependence on imported construction materials and lack of domestic suppliers for 220kV components expose the project to supply chain delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize international competitive bidding, conduct supply market intelligence, and actively monitor material procurement lead times.
gen_risks.evidence: The construction sector in Mongolia has been heavily reliant on imports, with statistics showing that 75-80% of construction materials are sourced from outside the country.

gen_risks.description: Extreme climate hazards including severe cold, heavy snow, freezing, high winds, and flooding pose risks of structural damage to transmission lines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate resilient engineering design standards for towers and insulators considering maximum wind loads, extreme cold, and flood risks.
gen_risks.evidence: Mongolia is prone to risks from climate hazards such as flooding, wildfires, and landslides, with exposure to drought and extreme cold

gen_risks.description: Workers face severe occupational health and safety hazards during civil works, including electrocution, falling from height, and tower collapse risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce Labor Management Procedures, adopt World Bank Group EHS Guidelines, and implement mandatory high-altitude and live-line safety protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: occupational health and safety (OHS) risks associated with live power lines, working at height, electric and magnetic fields (EMF)

gen_risks.description: Gender-based workplace biases and obstacles constrain women's employment and career advancement in technical and managerial roles at the transmission utility.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a workforce gender gap assessment, adopt gender-responsive HR policies, provide female leadership training, and track gender target indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: gender-based biases may be an obstacle to women’s employment and especially to career progression at NPTG.

gen_risks.description: Civil works during line construction may cause temporary restrictions on access to pastureland, wells, and resources for local herder communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Resettlement Policy Framework and Stakeholder Engagement Plan, conducting consultations and utilizing the project Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders (for example, pasture, wells, etc.) and sensitive receptors

gen_risks.description: Evaluation Committee members' unfamiliarity with English bidding documents and World Bank procurement regulations risks delays in contract awards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted World Bank procurement training to Evaluation Committee staff and establish clear decision-making workflows in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: The Evaluation Committee members normally do not have knowledge and experience in handling English documents, and it may cause delays with the evaluation process.

gen_risks.description: High prevalence of unqualified construction materials in the local market risks compromising the quality and safety of transmission infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply rated evaluation criteria to assess bidders' material quality control strategies and mandate strict material testing protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market.

gen_risks.description: Government election cycles and frequent turnover of decision-making officials risk disrupting PMO staffing continuity and delaying key approvals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactively engage re-elected or new government officials, formalize PMO staffing decrees, and institutionalize project implementation arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential changes in Government officials involved in project activities due to election cycle in first half year of next calendar year

gen_risks.description: Lack of transmission line redundancy on key power corridors leads to prolonged electricity supply outages and high network fault vulnerability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct a double-circuit 220kV transmission line to provide N-1 redundancy and strengthen network reliability in the Central Energy System.
gen_risks.evidence: due to the lack of redundancy of the power system, with only a single 110kV corridor in many parts of the system

gen_risks.description: Heavy reliance on electricity imports from Russia exposes Mongolia to cross-border supply vulnerabilities and energy security risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Expand domestic transmission network capacity to evacuate local renewable energy and reduce import dependency.
gen_risks.evidence: domestic generation was falling short of demand and Mongolia’s dependency on Russian imports reached almost 20 percent in 2022.

gen_risks.description: Complex Treasury fund-flow processes involving MNT investment sub-accounts create potential disbursement bottlenecks and payment delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize a clear Financial Management Manual, operate a segregated Designated Account, and streamline Treasury disbursement review procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays and bottlenecks in the project funds flow arrangements that got complicated with the addition of an investment project account within the Treasury

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risks are rated Substantial. The parliamentary election was held in June 2024 and a new coalition government was formed, with representation of all three major political parties. While there may be risks of disagreement on the approval of individual projects, these risks will be mitigated by the strong alignment of the proposed operation with the NRP and the new Government Action Plan for 2024-2028.
gt_risks.mitigation: Continued engagement with key stakeholders, including government and the parliament, through ongoing analytical and technical support on VRE integration and energy sector reform, will help mitigate risks going forward. The Development Partner Group, co-chaired by the World Bank and UNDP, will also offer a donor coordination platform to maintain political momentum for RE integration.

gt_risks.description: The macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. Mongolia's economic outlook is dependent on global macroeconomic factors, in particular commodity prices. Despite recent positive short-term developments from coal and agricultural exports, Mongolia still needs to strengthen fiscal and external buffers to respond to future shocks and continue reforms aimed at diversifying the economy.
gt_risks.mitigation: To mitigate these risks and manage external balances, the World Bank has been, and will continue to be, supporting the authorities in restoring fiscal and external buffers through analytical and advisory work.

gt_risks.description: The sector strategies and policies risk is rated Substantial. Substantial risk still exists due to institutional fragmentation, lack of policies to promote RE projects, and lack of clear commitment of reforms, especially related to tariff reforms that are crucial to make the sector viable and be able to refinance projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include actively engaging in multi-stakeholder coordination meetings and providing technical advice and capacity building to key stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: The institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk is rated Substantial. The implementing agency MOE and NPTG have experience implementing World Bank-funded projects; however, there is a substantial risk that newly hired PMO staff may not have sufficient capacity, which could potentially lead to implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The PMO will be strengthened with experienced consultants and targeted training and capacity building. Mitigating measures include the World Bank's scrutiny of PMO members' selection, including a review of the TOR and providing no objection to the qualification criteria of the staff.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. There are substantial risks due to the reliance of MOE on a newly constituted PMO, which may cause delays in processing payments, conducting IFRs, and other reporting requirements; the construction sector in Mongolia is often subject to delays and cost overruns. Potential procurement risks include (i) likelihood of time and cost overruns due to weak contract management capacity, and (ii) significant procurement delays due to delayed initiation of procurement and establishment of needed staffing arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: Capacity building through customized training and TA is a central element of the Project, along with strong project supervision and contract management capacity building; MOE will continue to directly provide intensive support to the PMO. Procurement risks are mitigated by (a) establishing a PMO with appropriate procurement and technical staff per FIDIC contract standards; (b) clearly defined workflow in decision-making within the MOE/PMO procurement manual; and (c) extensive market engagement to stimulate market participation.
